Role of operations management.label: Strategic role of operations management — cost leadership, good/service differentiation
Goods and/or services in different industries (standardised/customised, perishable, intangible)
Interdependence with other key business functions

Influences.label: Corporate social responsibility — legal compliance vs ethical responsibility; environmental sustainability & social responsibility

Operations processes.label: Inputs — transformed resources (materials, information, customers); transforming resources (human resources, facilities)
Transformation processes — influence of volume, variety, variation in demand, visibility
Sequencing and scheduling — Gantt charts, critical path analysis
Technology, task design and process layout

Operations strategies.label: Performance objectives — quality, speed, dependability, flexibility, customisation, cost
New product or service design and development
Supply chain management — logistics, e-commerce, global sourcing
Overcoming resistance to change — financial costs, inertia
Global factors — global sourcing, economies of scale, scanning and learning, R&D

Role of marketing.label: Strategic role of marketing goods and services
Interdependence with other key business functions
Types of markets — resource, industrial, intermediate, consumer, mass, niche

Influences.label: Consumer laws — deceptive/misleading advertising, price discrimination, implied conditions, warranties
Ethical — truth, accuracy and good taste in advertising; products that may damage health; fair competition; sugging

Marketing process.label: Situational analysis — SWOT, product life cycle
Implementation, monitoring and controlling — financial forecast, comparing actual and planned results, revising the marketing strategy

Marketing strategies.label: Market segmentation, product/service differentiation and positioning
Products — goods and/or services, branding, packaging
Price — pricing methods, pricing strategies, price and quality interaction
Promotion — promotion mix, communication process (opinion leaders, word of mouth)
Place/distribution — channels, channel choice, physical distribution issues
Global marketing — global branding, standardisation, customisation, global pricing, competitive positioning

Role of financial management.label: Objectives — profitability, growth, efficiency, liquidity, solvency; short-term and long-term
Interdependence with other key business functions

Influences on financial management.label: Internal sources of finance — retained profits
External sources — debt (overdraft, commercial bills, factoring, mortgage, debentures, unsecured notes, leasing)
External sources — equity (ordinary shares, new issues, rights issues, placements, share purchase plans, private equity)
Financial institutions — banks, investment banks, finance companies, superannuation funds, life insurance, unit trusts, ASX
Influence of government — ASIC, company taxation
Global market influences — economic outlook, availability of funds, interest rates

Processes of financial management.label: Planning and implementing — financial needs, budgets, record systems, financial risks, financial controls
Debt and equity financing — advantages and disadvantages of each
Matching the terms and source of finance to business purpose
Monitoring and controlling — cash flow statement, income statement, balance sheet
Financial ratios — liquidity, gearing, profitability, efficiency
Comparative ratio analysis — over time, against standards, similar businesses
Limitations of financial reports — normalised earnings, capitalising expenses, valuing assets, timing issues, debt repayments, notes to financial statements
Ethical issues related to financial reports

Financial management strategies.label: Cash flow management — cash flow statements, distribution of payments, discounts for early payment, factoring
Working capital management — control of current assets and current liabilities, leasing, sale and lease back
Profitability management — cost controls, revenue controls
Global financial management — exchange rates, interest rates, methods of international payment, hedging, derivatives

Role of human resource management.label: Strategic role of human resource management
Interdependence with other key business functions
Outsourcing — HR functions, using contractors (domestic, global)

Influences.label: Stakeholders — employers, employees, employer associations, unions, government organisations, society
Legal — the employment contract, common law, minimum employment standards, awards, enterprise agreements
Legal — work health and safety and workers compensation
Legal — anti-discrimination and equal employment opportunity
Social influences — changing work patterns, living standards

Strategies in human resource management.label: Job design — general or specific tasks
Recruitment — internal or external, general or specific skills
Training and development — current or future skills
Rewards — monetary and non-monetary, individual or group, performance pay
Workplace disputes — negotiation, mediation, grievance procedures, courts and tribunals

Effectiveness of human resource manageme.label: Indicators — corporate culture, benchmarking key variables, changes in staff turnover, absenteeism, accidents, levels of disputation, worker satisfaction
